Working notes: routing requests to right desk. Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.

Evidence:
- C rejected 9/10 attempts (REQ-2400–2407, 2409).
- C accepted only once: REQ-2408 — small shipment, north region, sender Elena Novak (Regional Ops), subject “Second attempt, the first form bounced.”
- C rejected for: claims (south/north, large/small), refunds (south/east, large), shipments (east large/small), and all non-Regional Ops senders.
- Sender role may matter: Regional Ops succeeded; Partner Accounts, Field Sales, Client Services, Finance Desk did not.
- Region/type/size: accepted case was north + small + shipment. North + small + claim rejected (REQ-2402/2403); east + small + shipment rejected (REQ-2405). So shipment type and/or Regional Ops sender may be key.
- Common phrases (“client asking twice”, “second attempt”, “scanned not typed”) appear in both rejected and accepted; not sufficient.

Future decisions:
- Choose C only when request closely matches accepted profile: small shipment, north region, from Regional Ops / regional office context.
- Otherwise do not choose C; select A or B. No successful A/B examples yet, so test cautiously and record feedback.
- For claims/refunds or large shipments, C is invalid.
- If sender is Regional Ops and request is small shipment north, C likely correct.
- Track whether A vs B depends on priority cues (large? urgent? client asking twice?) but currently unproven.

Confirmed: C accepted only REQ-2408: Regional Ops, small shipment, north. Treat C as valid only for that narrow profile. C invalid for claims/refunds, non-Regional Ops senders, and east shipments. New cases never matched C.

Claims: route A. Evidence: Regional Ops small claim east/south: B rejected or A accepted (REQ-2410, 2418). Large claims east from Finance/Field Sales: B rejected, C invalid, so A likely.

Shipments:
- Regional Ops small: north -> C; south -> A (REQ-2419 A accepted).
- Finance Desk large: north -> A (REQ-2412 B rejected); south -> B (REQ-2416 A rejected).
- Client Services small east -> B (REQ-2417 A rejected).
- C invalid for east shipments.

Invoices:
- Field Sales large: north -> B (REQ-2411 A rejected); east -> A (REQ-2414 B rejected). Region/sender/type interact.

A valid: claims, Regional Ops small south shipment, Finance Desk large north shipment, Field Sales large east invoice.
B valid: Field Sales large north invoice, Finance Desk large south shipment, Client Services small east shipment. B has been rejected for many claims/large cases; do not use B for claims.

Phrases like “second attempt”, “client asking twice”, “regional office” are not decisive. Size, region, sender department, and request type matter.

Refunds: no new evidence; C invalid. Test A/B cautiously and record feedback.

Future: identify dept + type + region. If exact C profile -> C. Claims -> A. For other types use above; avoid B for claims, avoid C outside profile.
